Preface
The intent of the System Impact Study is to determine a plan, with approximate cost and
construction time estimates, to connect the subject generation interconnection project to the PJM
network at a location specified by the Interconnection Customer. As a requirement for
interconnection, the Interconnection Customer may be responsible for the cost of constructing:
Network Upgrades, which are facility additions, or upgrades to existing facilities, that are needed
to maintain the reliability of the PJM system. All facilities required for interconnection of a
generation interconnection project must be designed to meet the technical specifications (on PJM
web site) for the appropriate transmission owner.
In some instances an Interconnection Customer may not be responsible for 100% of the
identified network upgrade cost because other transmission network uses, e.g. another generation
interconnection or merchant transmission upgrade, may also contribute to the need for the same
network reinforcement. The possibility of sharing the reinforcement costs with other projects
may be identified in the Feasibility Study, but the actual allocation will be deferred until the
System Impact Study is performed.
The System Impact Study estimates do not include the feasibility, cost, or time required to obtain
property rights and permits for construction of the required facilities. The project developer is
responsible for the right of way, real estate, and construction permit issues. For properties
currently owned by Transmission Owners, the costs may be included in the study.
General
Mason Dixon, LLC (“Interconnection Customer”) has proposed an incremental increase – uprate
– to prior queue project AB2-038 wind generation facility located in the areas of Big Savage and
Little Savage Mountains, Somerset County, Pennsylvania. The increased capability associated
with this queue request AB2-041 is achieved by adding six more new wind turbines to the 19 of
previous queue project AB2-038.

AB2-038 Mason Dixon LLC Queue Request changed ownership from Big Savage LLC to

The proposed in-service date for the AB2-041 project is December 15, 2019. This study does
not imply a Potomac Edison (“Transmission Owner”) commitment to this in-service date.
Point of Interconnection
This project will interconnect with the Potomac Edison transmission system at same existing POI
from previous projects U2-073/Z2-013 and AB2-038. This POI is a direct injection into
Frostburg Substation 138 kV bus. Refer to Appendix 2 for a one-line diagram of system
configuration.

Executive Summary
Generator interconnection request U2-073/AB2-038 is for a 200 MW Maximum Facility Output
(MFO) wind generating facility. U2-073/AB2-038 consists of 68 x 2.05 MW Senvion MM92
Turbines and 19 x 3.2 MW Senvion MM122 Turbines with the Point of Interconnection (POI) at
the Frostburg 138 kV substation. The facility is located in the First Energy (FE) transmission
system, Allegany County, Maryland.
Generator interconnection request AB2-041 is for a 19.2 MW Maximum Facility Output (MFO)
wind generating facility. AB2-041 consists of 6 x 3.2 MW Senvion MM122 Turbines with the
Point of Interconnection (POI) at the Frostburg 138 kV substation. The facility is located in the
First Energy (FE) transmission system, Allegany County, Maryland.
This report describes a dynamic simulation analysis of U2-073/AB2-038 and AB2-041 queue
projects as part of the overall system impact study.
The power flow scenario for the analysis was based on the RTEP 2020 summer peak load case,
modified to include applicable queue projects. U2-073/AB2-038 and AB2-041 has been
dispatched online at maximum power output, with approximately unity power factor at the high-
side of the station transformer.
U2-073/AB2-038 and AB2-041 was tested for compliance with NERC, PJM, Transmission
Owner and other applicable criteria. For this study, 58 contingencies were simulated, each with a
10 second simulation time period. Studied faults included:
 Steady-state operation (20 second simulation)
 Three-phase faults with normal clearing time
 Single-phase bus faults
 Single-phase faults with a stuck breaker
 Single phase faults with delayed (Zone 2) clearing at remote end due to primary relaying
failure
 Single-phase faults with loss of multiple-circuit tower line
All other contingencies met the recovery criteria:
 The U2-073/AB2-038 and AB2-041 generators were able to ride through the faults
except for faults where protective actions trip one or more generator(s).
 All generators maintained synchronism and any post-contingency oscillations are
positively damped with a damping margin of at least 3%.
 All bus voltages recover to 0.7 p.u. within 2.5 seconds and the final voltage is within the
range of 0.92 p.u. to 1.05 p.u. Note no final voltage violations less than 0.95 p.u. were
observed.
 No transmission element trips, other than those either directly connected or designated to
trip as a consequence of the fault.

1. Introduction
Generator interconnection request U2-073/AB2-038 is for a 200 MW Maximum Facility Output
(MFO) wind generating facility. U2-073/AB2-038 consists of 68 x 2.05 MW Senvion MM92
Turbines and 19 x 3.2 MW Senvion MM122 Turbines with the Point of Interconnection (POI) at
the Frostburg 138 kV substation. The facility is located in the First Energy (FE) transmission
system, Allegany County, Maryland.
Generator interconnection request AB2-041 is for a 19.2 MW Maximum Facility Output (MFO)
wind generating facility. AB2-041 consists of 6 x 3.2 MW Senvion MM122 Turbines with the
Point of Interconnection (POI) at the Frostburg 138 kV substation. The facility is located in the
First Energy (FE) transmission system, Allegany County, Maryland.
This analysis is effectively a screening study to determine whether the addition of U2-073/AB2-
038 and AB2-041 will meet the dynamic requirements of the NERC, PJM and Transmission
Owner reliability standards.
This report describes the following:
 A description of the U2-073/AB2-038 and AB2-041 project and how it is proposed to be
connected to the grid
 A description of how the project is modeled in this study
 A description of the fault cases analyzed in this study
 A discussion of the results.

2. Description of the Project
U2-073 consists of 68 x 2.05 MW Senvion MM92 turbines each connected to a 34.5/0.69 kV
step up transformer, all of which are connected to the 138/34.5 kV Generator Step Up
transformer (GSU) of 96/128/160 MVA rating.
AB2-038 consists of 19 x 3.2 MW Senvion MM122 turbines each connected to a 34.5/0.56 kV
step up transformer of 3.8 MVA rating each, all of which are connected with a 138/34.5 kV
Generator Step Up transformer 54/72/90 MVA rating.
AB2-041 consists of 6 x 3.2 MW Senvion MM122 turbines each connected to a 34.5/0.56 kV
step up transformer of 3.8 MVA rating each. The AB2-041 connects to the 138 kV bus through
the same 138/34.5 kV GSU transformer as AB2-038.
Both generation sites are connected via same 8.31 mile generation tie line to the POI in
Frostburg Substation at the 138 kV bus. Please refer to Figure 1 for a one-line diagram of the
generation.

3. Loadflow and Dynamics Case Setup
The dynamic simulation analysis was performed using PSS/E Version 33.10.0.
The power flow scenario and fault cases for this study are based on PJM’s Regional
Transmission Planning Process1.
The selected power flow scenario is the RTEP 2020 summer peak load case with the following
modifications:
 Addition of all applicable queue projects prior to U2-073/AB2-083 and AB2-041.
 Addition of the U2-073/AB2-038 and AB2-041 queue project.
 Dispatch of units within 5 buses of the POI of the U2-073/AB2-038 and AB2-041 queue
project.
o Generators set to their maximum power output.
o The reactive power output of each unit set near unity power factor at the high side
of the station transformer.

4. Fault Cases
Tables 5 through 10 list the contingencies that were studied, with representative worst case total
clearing times provided by PJM. Each contingency was studied over a 10 second simulation time
interval.
The studied contingencies include:
 Steady-state operation (20 second simulation)
 Three-phase faults with normal clearing time
 Single-phase bus faults
 Single-phase faults with a stuck breaker
 Single phase faults with delayed (Zone 2) clearing at remote end due to primary relaying
failure
 Single-phase faults with loss of multiple-circuit tower line
Contingencies were created for the following buses:
 Frostburg 138 kV
 U2-030 TAP 138 kV
 Z2-038 TAP 138 kV
 Ridgeley 138 kV
 Cumberland 138 kV
 AA1-107 138 kV
Clearing times were modeled based on PJM’s “2017 Revised Clearing times for each PJM
company” spreadsheet revision 20. Note FE Area 201 normal clearing times for 138 kV lines
were specified as 6 or 8 to 12 cycles. All normal clearing times were initally examined as 12
cycles. If violations were observed the clearing time was reduced to 6 cycles.
Attachment 2 contains one-line diagrams of the FE network in the vicinity of U2-073/AB2-038
and AB2-041, showing where faults were applied.
The positive sequence fault impedances for single-phase faults were modeled using a zero
sequence to positive sequence impedance ratio of 0.3 for FE’s area derived from a separate short-
circuit case. The ratio was applied to the posive sequence value in PSS/E and the single-phase
fault impedance was calculated.

5. Evaluation Criteria
This study is focused on U2-073/AB2-038 and AB2-041, along with the rest of the PJM system,
maintaining synchronism and having all states return to an acceptable new condition following
the disturbance. The recovery criteria applicable to this study are as per PJM’s Regional
Transmission Planning Process and Transmission Owner criteria:
 The U2-073/AB2-038 and AB2-041 generators were able to ride through the faults
except for faults where protective actions trip one or more generator(s).
 All generators maintained synchronism and any post-contingency oscillations are
positively damped with a damping margin of at least 3%.
 All bus voltages recover to 0.7 p.u. within 2.5 seconds and the final voltage is within the
range of 0.92 p.u. to 1.05 p.u. Note no final voltage violations less than 0.95 p.u. were
observed.
 No transmission element trips, other than those either directly connected or designated to
trip as a consequence of the fault.

6. Summary of Results
Plots from the dynamic simulations are provided in Attachment 6 with results summarized in
Tables 5 through 10.
Final bus voltage violations under 0.92 p.u. were observed with that addition of the U2-
073/AB2-038 and AB2-041 queue projects. Table 11 summarizes the voltage violations
observed with the addition of the AB2-041 queue project.
The normal clearing times was reduced from 12 cycles to 6 cycles but did not resolve the voltage
violations. Comments were provided in PJM’s “2017 Revised Clearing times for each PJM
company” spreadsheet revision 20 stating the typical clearing time was 6 cycles but could be as
long as 8 to 12 cycles if electro-mechanical negative sequence direct ground relays are installed.
